what_it_is.prose: RUAG is a Swiss aerospace and defence technology group. Its relevance to the India military-aerospace Atlas is through the Dornier Do-228 lineage rather than any direct Indian order or joint venture. After the Dornier and Fairchild-Dornier eras, RUAG obtained Do-228 production rights in 2002 and acquired the aircraft's type certificate in 2003, becoming the design-authority holder. RUAG launched the modernised Do-228 New Generation (certified 2010), and under RUAG's manufacturing model the fuselage, wings and tail assemblies were built by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) at Kanpur and shipped to Oberpfaffenhofen, Germany, for final assembly — HAL agreeing a roughly €80 million, ten-year structures supply contract at the 2008 Berlin Air Show. This is the same HAL Kanpur line that licence-produces the Do-228 for the Indian armed forces (Atlas slug do228). RUAG sold the Do-228 production line and type certificate to General Atomics (announced 2020, completed February 2021), so the current design authority no longer rests with RUAG. This compact Tier C card records RUAG's Do-228 design-lineage and HAL-supply link honestly, without asserting a standalone Indian contract or footprint for RUAG itself.

open_questions: RUAG has no direct Indian defence contract or JV; its India link is the Do-228 type-certificate lineage and the historical HAL structures-supply relationship
Since 2020-21 the Do-228 type certificate and production line sit with General Atomics AeroTec Systems, not RUAG
